title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Paired Shared-Initial Candidate Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (CAND-2026-001) that measured the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) on deterministic-invariant acceptance for intent→configuration NetOps tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we executed N=200 preregistered tasks with the hosted model declared as gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset). Provider-call accounting shows 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair (201 model calls). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). The paired contingency counts are n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The exact two-sided McNemar p-value (exact-binomial two-sided convention) equals 1.0; the paired-bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single observed improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a required-sequence (multi-step ordering) violation in an extreme-difficulty task. We report the preregistration, complete execution accounting (start/end timestamps, model-call audit), the confirmatory paired analysis, representative difficulty diagnostics, and artifact-grounded failure-mode interpretation. All claims about execution, counts, and traces are grounded in the archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as synthesis engines that translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness in such pipelines requires that generated artifacts satisfy deterministic invariants—syntactic well-formedness, required sequence/orderings for multi-device changes, group-level constraints (minimum/maximum active interfaces), and policy-level constraints such as isolation or waypointing. Recent prototype systems and benchmarks show feasibility of intent→configuration workflows, but open empirical questions remain about how much gated verification and bounded automated repair change acceptance rates when the identical initial candidate generation is reused across comparison conditions.

This study isolates the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair on an identical sampled candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the same single sampled candidate per task was deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes; consequently any paired difference can only arise from the deterministic verifier and the single permitted repair. Our primary estimand is the paired difference in per-task binary acceptance by a deterministic verifier (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The shared-initial paired design therefore measures a repair-only effect and does not evaluate alternative guarded designs that obtain independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompting, or multi-sample selection.
sections.related_work:
Prior work demonstrates active research in LLM-driven intent→configuration pipelines and in tool-augmented architectures that combine generators with validators or external solvers. NetConfEval and related intent→configuration prototypes document generation-based translations of intent into device configurations and motivate verifier-aware evaluation [1]. Deterministic network verification approaches provide operational oracles for syntactic and semantic invariants and are a natural evaluation substrate for configuration synthesis [2]. Work on generate→validate→repair in adjacent domains—automated program repair and test-in-the-loop patching—provides a methodological precedent for guarded pipelines and motivates bounded, validator-triggered repairs, though those demonstrations are primarily software-centric and do not directly quantify NetOps-specific sequencing or group-constraint effects [4].

Recent surveys and methodological reviews highlight (i) the rapid emergence of tool-augmented agentic designs that grant LLMs controlled access to external solvers or validators, (ii) practical failure modes (hallucination, adversarial contamination) that motivate verification and provenance controls, and (iii) reporting guidelines recommending preregistration and artifacted evaluation for LLM studies [3],[6],[5]. Synthesizing the verified literature yields three relevant facts: (a) intent→configuration pipelines are actively prototyped and benchmarked [1]; (b) deterministic verifiers are an appropriate operational oracle for configuration correctness evaluation [2]; and (c) guarded generate→validate→repair patterns are a promising architectural design demonstrated in adjacent domains but require NetOps-specific controlled experiments to quantify repair-only effects in multi-device sequencing contexts [4],[6]. Our paired, shared_initial_candidate experiment addresses the narrower empirical gap of measuring the marginal repair effect when identical initial candidates are reused.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The full experiment and analysis plan were preregistered as CAND-2026-001 before any model calls. The preregistration fixed a paired binary estimand that compares per-task deterministic-verifier acceptance under baseline (no repair) versus guarded (verifier may trigger ≤1 repair) conditions, task_count=200, generation_semantics=shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both episodes), and maximum one automated repair call per task. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial-tail convention) computed from discordant pair counts; we predeclared a paired-bootstrap (percentile) CI procedure (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for the paired absolute risk difference.

Deterministic task generation and verifier oracle. Tasks were produced by a deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) and selected by a fixed index rule in the preregistration. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (an explicit ordered list of per-interface field assignments), allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies (final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields, protected_interfaces). The deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is the operational oracle: it parses generated commands, enforces allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, checks required_sequence ordering, evaluates group-level invariants, and returns a boolean full_intent_constraint_validation only when all encoded constraints are satisfied. The verifier emits structured tracer output (validation_before, validation_after, violation_codes, repair_applied) that we used as authoritative scoring evidence; those tracer outputs are archived and cited in Results.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics, sanitizer, and repair policy. The adapter contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair the exact same initial generation (a single sampled candidate) was supplied to both baseline and guarded episodes. A deterministic formatting sanitizer ran before verifier parsing to fix minor formatting issues. If the verifier reported invariant violations the guarded logic could invoke at most one automated repair call to the hosted model; the repair prompt was constructed deterministically from the validator trace per the preregistered templates. Repair calls were counted against the maximum_model_calls budget and recorded in the execution manifest. Because the archived model-configuration record declares temperature = null (unset), we explicitly note that a null/unset temperature does not constitute evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and must not be interpreted as temperature=0; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling therefore remains a possible background property, even though the experiment used exactly one initial sample per pair by design.

Provider-call and execution accounting. The execution manifest records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1; cache_miss_count = 201 and cache_hit_count = 0 document fresh model generations for all shared-initial calls and the single repair-stage call. Start and end timestamps show run elapsed ≈29 minutes (start 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00, end 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00). All execution, model-configuration, verifier logs, provider traces, and analysis parameters are archived in the execution bundle.
sections.results:
Execution and confirmatory analysis. Execution completed with planned_episode_count = 400 and completed_episode_count = 400; no episodes failed or were excluded. Confirmatory counts from the archived analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) are: complete_pairs = 200, baseline_success_count = 199 (baseline success_rate = 0.995), guarded_success_count = 200 (guarded success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11=199, n10=1 (guarded success, baseline failure), n01=0, n00=0. The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0050000000000000044. With n = n10 + n01 = 1 and k = n10 = 1 the exact two-sided McNemar p-value computed by the exact-binomial-tail convention equals p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the absolute difference with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729) equals [0.00, 0.015]. These numeric artifacts and the analysis log reproduce from the archived raw results when the analysis executor is re-run.

Single repair event and localized diagnostic. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair across all pairs. Archived validator traces for the repaired pair show that the shared initial candidate violated the task's required_sequence ordering constraint; the task's difficulty metadata recorded required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3, and difficulty.level = "extreme". The verifier tracer documents validation_before.violation_codes identifying a required-sequence ordering breach and validation_after.valid = true once the bounded repair was applied; repair_applied was set true in the tracer and the scorer returned score = 1 with score_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION". The repair therefore converted an ordering-dependency failure into a configuration accepted by the deterministic verifier. The archived tracer fields constitute the evidence that the single observed paired improvement resulted from an authorized verifier-triggered repair that effected a permitted reordering.

Difficulty diagnostics and exploratory observations. Representative task manifests in the archived bundle encode difficulty metadata; in the representative subset required_command_count spans 3–9 and changed_interface_count reaches 3, with explicit task patterns labeled "very_hard" and "extreme". The single baseline failure (the repaired pair) associates with an extreme composite-difficulty profile (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3), consistent with our preregistered exploratory hypothesis that multi-device sequencing and dependency complexity concentrate residual failures. No persistent unparsables, preregistered exclusions, or contamination flags were recorded.

Quantitative uncertainty and interpretation. The observed baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) places the confirmatory test in a sparse-discordant regime: only one discordant pair yields limited directional evidence under an exact-binomial McNemar convention (p = 1.0). The paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] quantifies the upper bound of plausible absolute improvement attributable to the repair-only estimand; under the shared_initial_candidate design the data are compatible with at most a small absolute improvement (≤1.5 percentage points) due to bounded repair in this experimental setting. In other words, the experiment provides artifact-backed evidence that bounded verifier-triggered repair can correct at least some localized ordering faults expressed in the verifier's invariants, but the realized high baseline leaves the confirmatory test underpowered for detecting modest absolute improvements.
sections.discussion:
What this paired shared-initial estimand measures. Because baseline and guarded conditions begin from the identical sampled candidate per pair, any paired difference isolates the marginal effect of permitting an automated verifier-triggered repair. The realized estimand therefore answers a narrow operational question: given the same initial generation, how often does a single bounded validator-derived repair convert an invalid configuration into one that satisfies all encoded deterministic invariants?

Interpretation of the observed outcome. The archived evidence shows one such conversion in 200 tasks. The diagnostic tracer indicates an ordering dependency correction in an extreme task (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3). That concrete artifact supports the specific mechanistic claim that a validator-constructed repair prompt can effect a reordering sufficient to satisfy required_sequence constraints as encoded in the manifest. The overall numerical effect is small in absolute terms (0.5 percentage points) and the paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (0.015) quantifies that, under our repair-only estimand, large absolute gains are incompatible with these data.

Statistical regime, power implications, and ceiling effects. The preregistered power rationale targeted detection of moderate absolute paired increases (~10–15 percentage points) for N = 200 under mid-range baseline assumptions (baseline ≈45–65%). The unexpectedly high baseline pass rate (99.5%) produced a ceiling effect that materially reduced realized sensitivity for the predeclared effect sizes. With only one discordant pair the two-sided exact McNemar p-value conveys no directional significance (p = 1.0) under the exact-tail convention used; the paired-bootstrap CI, however, provides a useful bound on plausible improvement magnitudes. Researchers designing future confirmatory tests of repair-only estimands should (a) account for the possibility of high baseline accuracy and plan for larger N or stratified sampling of higher-difficulty tasks, or (b) change the estimand to compare independent guarded-first-pass generations (not shared_initial_candidate) if the object is to measure guarded prompting or multi-sample selection gains rather than repair-only effects.

Failure-mode insight and verifier scope. The deterministic verifier enforces encoded ordering and group-level invariants that are expressible in the task manifests (required_sequence, minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields). The archived failure-mode tracer shows that reordering is a practical repair target when the failure manifests as an explicit required_sequence violation. The verifier does not emulate dataplane forwarding, vendor runtime quirks, or time-dependent behaviors; therefore repairs that would only be detectable or validated through live dataplane emulation are outside the verifier's scope. Operational deployment would require additional emulation or staged canary runs before applying repaired configurations in production.

Threats to validity and limitations. Internal: the shared_initial_candidate paired design isolates repair-only effects but does not address model sampling variability, prompt sensitivity, or different guarded-pipeline first-pass behaviors. Construct: the deterministic verifier enforces a defined set of encoded invariants but is not a substitute for device- or dataplane-level testing. External: this run used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank; extrapolation to other models, retrieval-augmented pipelines, or live heterogeneous vendor stacks is limited. The preregistered missingness and contamination plans recorded no exclusions, no persistent unparsables, and no contamination flags; deterministic reconciliation shows pair_accounting_consistent = true. These are strengths for internal reproducibility but do not remove external-generalizability constraints.

Operational implications and future directions. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a narrowly scoped operational conclusion: in this synthetic deterministic task bank with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and a single-model run, a verifier-triggered bounded repair corrected a localized multi-step ordering fault in one extreme task. This supports the practice of coupling generators to verifiers and permitting bounded, validator-driven repair when the invariants of interest are fully encoded in a verifier. Broader operational claims—improved operator triage time, multi-model robustness, adversarial resilience, or dataplane-correctness guarantees—were not measured and therefore remain to be evaluated by studies that incorporate live emulation, multiple independent guarded generations, adversarial contamination testing, and multi-model comparisons.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment to measure the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In 200 deterministic synthetic tasks with the hosted model declared as gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation in an extreme-difficulty task. Paired absolute risk difference = 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. Artifact-grounded evidence therefore supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded bounded repair can correct localized ordering/dependency faults that are expressible in the verifier's invariants in this synthetic verifier-backed setting. Broader operational claims require additional experiments (multi-model studies, independent-first-pass guarded semantics, adversarial contamination testing, and live-device/dataplane emulation).

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier (oracle): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Archived provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are available in the execution bundle for audit.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
